title: How to find out why trials don't buy: 11 cheap ways to collect lost-sales feedback in a day
summary: Jason Cohen argues the top way to raise revenue is learning why the 99.9% of prospects who look but don't buy walk away, not talking only to existing customers. He lists eleven low-effort tactics, such as optional download forms, paying for lost-sale interviews, uninstaller surveys, and free licenses in exchange for feedback sessions.

principles.text: Existing customers can't explain lost sales; you need feedback from the far larger group of prospects who didn't buy.
principles.quote: talking to existing customers isn't good enough! They bought in spite of your faults; you need to talk to the other 99.9% of your potential customers who aren't so forgiving and understanding.

principles.text: A short optional form before a download need not cut downloads, and without contact info you can't fix the funnel.
principles.quote: if a hundred people download in silence and don't buy, it doesn't matter that they downloaded.

principles.text: Collect opt-in emails from interested non-buyers even before you have a newsletter; they give you reasons to follow up later.
principles.quote: There's no reason not to build an honest, opt-in, no-spam list of people who are interested in your product.

principles.text: Pay lost-sale prospects (charity gift, coupon, swag, ~$25-50) for 15 minutes on why they didn't buy; run it until answers repeat or the budget runs out.
principles.quote: You don't have to offer it forever, just until you start hearing the same things over and over again. Or budget $1000 and run the offer until the budget is gone.

principles.text: Ask in-product at the moment of rejection (uninstaller, 'Complain' link, quit prompt) using a plain email or web form; most responses are noise but some are gold.
principles.quote: Sure, most of the time you'll get nothing and sometimes you'll get useless crap like "You suck," but sometimes you'll get gold.

principles.text: Give free licenses to non-buyers only in exchange for a feedback call; they weren't going to pay anyway, so you lose little.
principles.quote: You're not losing money on the sale because they weren't going to buy anyway.
